text: Reconcile discharge medicines against home medicines with a pharmacist, checking for duplicates, stopped medicines, and dose changes, and give the patient a clear updated medicine list.
Book a primary care follow-up visit within 7 days of discharge for high-risk patients, and within 14 days for medium-risk patients, and confirm the appointment before discharge.
Contact high-risk patients by phone within 48 hours of discharge to check symptoms, medicine understanding, and whether the follow-up visit is booked.

source: American Heart Association Heart Failure Guidance (summary)
text: For heart failure, monitor weight, fluid intake, and breathlessness daily, review diuretic medicines, and seek urgent care for rapid weight gain or worsening breathlessness.
For ischemic heart disease, ensure antiplatelet and statin medicines are reconciled at discharge, and arrange cardiology / primary care follow-up.
For COPD or asthma, check inhaler technique at discharge, review action plan for worsening breathlessness, and arrange respiratory / primary care follow-up.

source: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes (summary)
text: For diabetes, review glucose monitoring, hypoglycaemia signs, and diabetes medicines at discharge, and arrange diabetes / primary care follow-up.
Patients with multiple prior inpatient stays need a care transition plan with a named contact, a follow-up visit booked, and a medicine review, because prior stays are a strong predictor of return.
Give patients clear red-flag instructions: seek emergency care immediately for chest pain, severe breathlessness, or other emergency symptoms, do not wait for a scheduled follow-up call.
Provide discharge instructions in plain language, covering medicines, follow-up visits, activity, diet, and who to contact with questions, and confirm understanding with teach-back.
For pneumonia, ensure antibiotics and follow-up imaging / primary care review are arranged, and advise on return if fever or breathlessness worsens.
For kidney / urinary conditions, review medicines that affect kidney function, fluid advice, and primary care / nephrology follow-up as appropriate.
